display_name: Penfolds Bin 2 Mataro, South Eastern Australia
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Penfolds Bin 2 Mataro draws Shiraz and Mourvèdre from South Eastern Australia's coastal and inland sites, balancing peppery spice with dark fruit density. This bin-level blend skips Grange-level oak intensity for direct savory appeal. Drinkers get Northern Rhône restraint in an Australian frame at half the price of premium Shiraz.",
  "wine_summary": "Penfolds built its name on multi-regional blending, sourcing parcels across South Australia for Bin 2 Mataro to hit consistent dark fruit and meaty notes. Shiraz drives blackberry and black pepper from cooler McLaren Vale edges, while Mourvèdre adds olive tapenade depth. The 14.5% ABV across vintages like 2013 reflects warm-climate ripeness without excess heat, setting it apart from jammy Barossa singles.",
  "terroir_expression": "McLaren Vale's red-brown earth and terra rossa over limestone retain heat for Shiraz's blueberry and black plum ripeness, while rendzina soils contribute firm tannins that frame the wine's smoked meat edge. Dark cracking clays in wetter years like 2013 build structure against Gulf St Vincent's maritime cooling, yielding pepper from rotundone in Shiraz without overripe jam. Elevations from 50 to 350m add violet florals to the savory core.",
  "vinification_summary": "Penfolds ferments parcels separately before blending Shiraz and Mourvèdre, then matures in older American oak for 12 months to integrate spice without dominating fruit. This approach—multi-vineyard selection—ensures balance, as neutral oak lets dark cracking clay tannins shine. The result tastes meatier than straight Shiraz.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken: black pepper cuts spice, tannins grip fried crust. Lamb shank braised in red wine: savory Mourvèdre echoes meat reduction. Barbecued brisket: olive notes match smoke. Osso buco with gremolata: structure holds rich marrow. Cheeseburger with aged cheddar: dark fruit binds beef fat.",
  "comparable_wines": "Yalumba Old Acre Shiraz-Mourvèdre — similar South Australian GSM savory at value price. Tahbilk Shiraz-Mourvèdre — Nagambie Banks pepper matches Bin 2's restraint.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with grippy tannins and meaty savoriness",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink now through 2028 for vintages like 2013; store in cool darkness to soften tannins. Earlier bins like 2007 peak now.",
  "value_assessment": "$20-35 retail delivers Penfolds blending expertise. Torbreck Woodcutter's Shiraz and d'Arenberg The Stump Jump GSM compete at this price but lack the pepper focus. Buy it for reliable savory red without markup.",
  "market_position": "Casual drinkers grab Bin 2 from supermarket shelves for weeknight roasts. Australian restaurant lists pair it with grills at $50 markups. Collectors skip it for Grange, but exporters push it in Asia.",
  "insider_take": "Skip Bin 2 if you chase single-vineyard purity—its blend trades nuance for consistency. Barossa fans overlook the McLaren Vale pepper, missing the real draw. Stock up for anyone tired of fruit-bomb Shiraz.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,
